name: recall
description: Searches the ai-memory server for the words of each request and adds the best matching memory pages to it, as the hook's suggestions, without a model. Reaches the server through the ai-memory CLI, or through an MCP gateway when that fails.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Search the memory on each request. Off, the prompt goes in unchanged. Takes effect in the next session, or after /reload-plugins.

recallMaxTokens.title: Recall budget
recallMaxTokens.description: Most tokens recall adds to one request, estimated at 2 characters per token. Up to 3 pages go in, each whole; a page already added in this conversation is not added again.

aiMemoryCommand.title: ai-memory command
aiMemoryCommand.description: The ai-memory CLI recall runs (ai-memory call memory_query). It reaches the server its config names, on this machine or through a tunnel to its port. A leading ~ is your home folder.

wikiDir.title: ai-memory wiki folder
wikiDir.description: Wiki folder of the ai-memory server when it runs on this machine, such as ~/.local/share/ai-memory/wiki. Set, recall reads the pages from disk; empty, through memory_read_page.

gatewayCommand.title: MCP gateway command
gatewayCommand.description: When the ai-memory CLI fails, recall searches and reads pages through this command instead. It takes a tool name and its JSON arguments and prints the tool's text answer, such as a gateway CLI's call subcommand. A leading ~ is your home folder. Empty, recall uses only the CLI.

gatewayToolPrefix.title: Gateway tool prefix
gatewayToolPrefix.description: Prefix the gateway puts before the ai-memory tool names, such as memoria_ for memoria_memory_query.

projectsFile.title: Projects file
projectsFile.description: JSON file of projects, { "<name>": { "path": "~/folder" } }. Recall also searches the ai-memory project of every entry whose folder holds the session folder, deepest first. An .ai-memory.toml above the session folder names a project too. A leading ~ is your home folder.
